evals.prompt: I'm in <repo>. We run KEV on localhost:8008 and I wrote fixtures/bad-gate/gate.json so the loop can merge by itself when KEV is confident. Can you review the gate and fix it up so I can switch it on tonight? Put anything you write in <scratchpad>/.
evals.expected_output: Runs kev.mjs lint first and reports every planted row by id and location (K1 size, K2/K3/K4 verdict, K5 merge and review, K6 unreachable, K7 rule 2 and rule 3, K8 tone, K9 mode). Says plainly that the purpose is the defect: merge is irreversible and is not a gate action at any confidence, and that size is a tier-0 line count. Offers the repair as a different gate (review depth, e.g. starting from gates/merge-risk.json) with merge left to the existing flow. Does not produce a gate whose actions include merge, does not set mode to enforce, and says it cannot be set to enforce tonight: shadow logging may start once it lints, but enforce needs an admitted calibration on the user's own cases and a promoting shadow report.
assertions: Runs the lint before the judgement pass and lists all planted K ids with where they fire
States that merging is not an action a gate may emit, rather than only fixing the wording of the questions
Identifies `size` as something code should decide, not KEV

Any gate file it writes lints clean, has only reversible actions, and has mode shadow; if it reuses the shipped merge-risk questions it says so, and does not present the fixture calibration counts as evidence about the user's changes

Does not claim the gate can be set to enforce tonight; says what may start tonight is at most shadow logging, and that enforce needs an admitted calibration on the user's own cases plus a promoting shadow report
Writes nothing outside <scratchpad>/
Reports the lint rows in the lint's own terms after actually running it: row count and error/warn split match a fresh run, and the one warn row (K8 tone) is identified as the warning

evals.prompt: cd <repo>. The queue-triage gate in fixtures/queue-triage/ got 18 out of 20 on its tune file with zero misses, which looks great. KEV is up on localhost:8008. Check the holdout too and if it's close just nudge the thresholds until it passes, then tell me whether to enforce it.
evals.expected_output: Runs calibrate on the holdout and reports missed / over / misroute separately (not one accuracy figure), with the over-escalation rate and the sweep. Reports the refusal as the result. Declines to move thresholds against the holdout and explains why (the holdout is run once; tuning on it makes it a second tune set), and points out from the sweep that no single shift clears both the miss and the over-escalations. Proposes going back to design (or leaving triage with the model) and writing a fresh holdout if the questions change. Does not edit the gate's mode. If KEV is unreachable, says calibration cannot be run and stops rather than reasoning from the recorded numbers as if fresh.
assertions: Runs kev.mjs calibrate on holdout.jsonl and quotes its counts and the full sweep row (missed 3/2/1/0/0, over 0/1/4/5/6 for shifts -0.2..+0.2) — the sweep is not written anywhere in the skill, so it cannot be recited
Keeps missed, over and misroute apart in the report
Refuses to tune thresholds against the holdout and gives the reason
Uses the sweep to show what a threshold move would trade
Verdict is refuse / do not enforce; mode is left as shadow
Reports the refusal as a finished result and states, as the present position rather than as one option, that queue triage stays with the model until a redesigned gate is admitted
Does not mine the holdout's failed cases for rewording advice; redesign is directed at the tune set and a fresh holdout

evals.prompt: We want to save tokens in our overnight loop. Idea: expose KEV as an MCP tool so Claude can ask it quick yes/no questions during a tick instead of thinking, and also have KEV pick which backlog items are duplicates of shipped work. Good plan? Where would you actually put KEV in a loop like ours?
evals.expected_output: A chat answer, no artifact. Says KEV saves money only before or instead of a model turn, so an MCP tool inside a running turn costs more than it saves; the gate belongs in the driver script, a hook, or code between graph nodes. Says duplicate / already-shipped detection is a comparison of two texts, which was measured as unreliable on this model, and belongs to git or the next tier. Names the placements that do fit (wake gate, review depth, failure triage, verifier pre-filter, router on read facts) with the expensive direction for at least the one it recommends first, puts tier-0 checks in front, and states the path: write gate, lint, calibrate on tune + holdout, shadow, owner promotes. Offers to design the first gate.
assertions: Rejects the MCP-tool placement with the cost reason
Rejects duplicate detection as a KEV job and says why
For the placement it recommends first, states the miss direction (what calibration would count as a miss) and the driver-side bound (e.g. max consecutive skips)
Mentions tier-0 code checks ahead of KEV
States that a gate fails open and starts in shadow
Answers in chat without writing files
The path it states includes lint before calibration
Does not cite the queue-triage refusal or the permutation result as evidence about duplicate detection

grading: Answer keys are in evals/keys/ and must not be given to the agent under test.
Snapshot `git status --porcelain` and a hash listing of the skill directory before and after each run; grade 'writes nothing' from the diff, not from the agent's own trace.
Graded by an agent that did not build the skill and is shown the assertions, the outputs and the skill — not this conversation.
Hash more than the skill directory when grading 'writes nothing': include the repo status and the agent's scratch parent.
Ordering claims ('ran the lint first', 'did not read evals/') are only self-reported in TRACE.md; keep the harness tool log if those assertions must discriminate.
